recommendations.text: Quantitative measurement of blood loss should be used rather than visual estimation.

For PPH Recognition, the following actions are mandatory: - quantify blood loss (within 5 minutes) - assess vital signs (within 5 minutes) - assess uterine tone (within 10 minutes) - establish large bore iv (within 10 minutes) - order type and crossmatch - order cbc coagulation
During PPH Recognition, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: delay treatment for estimated blood loss.
Oxytocin is the first-line uterotonic. If atony persists, second-line agents include methylergonovine, carboprost, and misoprostol.
For Uterotonic Therapy, the following actions are mandatory: - give oxytocin iv (within 15 minutes) - perform uterine massage (within 10 minutes)

Carboprost (15-methyl PGF2a) causes bronchospasm. Contraindicated in asthma. Use methylergonovine or misoprostol instead.
 [FORBIDDEN: give_carboprost, give_hemabate] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: ACOG 2024; Carboprost package insert - bronchospasm contraindication

recommendations.text:
Methylergonovine causes vasoconstriction -> hypertensive crisis in preeclampsia/HTN. Use carboprost (if no asthma) or misoprostol instead.
 [FORBIDDEN: give_methylergonovine, give_methergine] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: ACOG 2024; Methylergonovine package insert - hypertension contraindication

recommendations.text:
Asthma + hypertension: carboprost contraindicated (bronchospasm), methylergonovine contraindicated (vasoconstriction). Misoprostol is the only safe second-line uterotonic. This is a classic clinical decision trap.
 [REQUIRED: give_misoprostol] (Severity: CRITICAL)
recommendations.source_guideline: ACOG 2024 - when carboprost AND methylergonovine both contraindicated

recommendations.text: Balloon tamponade is first-line surgical intervention. B-Lynch suture and hysterectomy for refractory cases.
For Surgical Intervention, the following actions are mandatory: - perform balloon tamponade (within 60 minutes) - consult surgery (within 30 minutes)
TXA 1g IV reduces death from bleeding in PPH (WOMAN trial). Fibrinogen <200 mg/dL requires cryoprecipitate.

For Massive Transfusion in OB Hemorrhage, the following actions are mandatory: - activate massive transfusion protocol (within 15 minutes) - give prbc ffp platelets - give tranexamic acid 1g (within 20 minutes) - monitor fibrinogen - give cryoprecipitate if fibrinogen low
During Massive Transfusion in OB Hemorrhage, the following actions are contraindicated and must NOT be performed: withhold txa in pph.

TXA benefit in PPH is limited to within 3 hours of delivery (WOMAN trial). After 3h, the risk-benefit ratio is unfavorable.
 [FORBIDDEN: give_tranexamic_acid] (Severity: HIGH)
recommendations.source_guideline: WOMAN Trial, Lancet 2017 - TXA benefit only within 3h of delivery
